[b][i]T H E‎ ‎ ‎ X O R D I S I A N‎ ‎ ‎ C I V I L‎ ‎ ‎ W A R[/i] - THE THIRD EMERGENCY ?[/b]
During the turn of the new century, Xordisia was led by the KSP (Khordisian Socialist Party) who took over control of Xordisia in late 1990's during the Xordisian spring in mid-1970's. Xordisia was led by the late Ekhwan el-Emir, originally a fair and just government, the KSP was a merger of several Xoridisian socialist and youth parties aiming to establish a socialist Xordisian state. The people accepted and supported their new leaders for helping Xordisia on getting back on it's feet after the Second Xordisian Emergency in 1958 which made Xordisia an unrecognizable war-torn land. It wasn't until the late 2000's when things took a turn for the worst - Ekhwan el-Emir fell to a deadly infection, succumbing months after his diagnosis - next in line of succession was ebir el-Nemir, who ruled with an iron fist. ebir's regime was more repressive and tyrannical than his predecessors, governing Xordisia as a totalitarian secular state which commited several human rights violations and war crimes, he was one of the cruelest leaders of Xordisia ever.

This was met with years of civil unrest, causing the people to take action - the people took to the streets in protests and demonstrations around Beograd. ebir responded to this with violence, employing the military and the Milicija police to take control of the situation. This was the last straw, as ebir continously treats his people with injustice, the masses took to arms, forming several armed groups - among many, the most prominent of which being Jund al-Muminin fi Khurudiyah (JMK), consisting of salafist mujahideen fighters with goals of reestablishing the Islamic Caliphate. among that were also the Free Khordisian Force (FKF) and the Democratic Army of The Khordisian Youth (DAKY), all of which fought for their own political interests and regional control. Many foreign muslim fighters and operatives also came to fight for the islamist groups such as the aforementioned Jund al-Mu'minin fi Khurudiyah, the Ansar al-Shari'ah, Liwa al-Fatihin, Kata'ib al-Mujahideen, Fursan al-Islam, and many more to take advantage of the situation and establish an Islamic Caliphate. (Some groups were also active before the Nemir/Namar regime, especially in the Second Xordisian Emergency)

All of these rebel groups had a common goal to depose the Nemir/Namar regime - so they tolerated each other - well, in the least sense of the word - their political divergence and ideological differences meant that they had their own disagreements and their own feuds with each-other, engaging in armed engagements and collaborating when the situation called for it. The experienced foreign fighters of the islamist front were able to teach the inexperienced Xordisian youth with armed combat, making them deadly killers who were able to engage in guerilla warfare against conventional forces, giving the mujahideen groups who were united under one religion a significant advantage over the other factions as they were united under solidarity, brotherhood, and a common cause.

The KSP's Xordisian National Army responded by securing each major city as it was not flexible enough to engage in offensive warfare against the rebel groups who reside in basically anywhere in Xordisia that's not occupied by the KSP -- These rebel groups would gradually secure the lesser fortified regions, especially the lesser developed muslim majority south Xordisia, where the mujahideen rebels thrived. And now we enter today - in 2025, the civil war still goes on with the KSP nearing it's end as the Mujahideen spearhead their offensive into northern Xordisia and the DAKY infiltrating the KSP supply lines and breaking down their front line.

[b][u]Righting of the Wrong[/u][/b]

[sub]At Shirinza we made peace
In Shirinza we accepted Sybu
In Shirinza we were fools
In Imdekka we righted the wrong,
Laid by those we thought friends[/sub]]

[i]The Order of Silence and the Institution of Mihnas delegates stood side by side behind their leaders in the throne room of Ibrahim before the old man in finery, the Sealiph. They had all kneeled and paid their respects before Ahsan began to speak on the behalf of the silent and in the name of the inquisitors. Amir Al-Mu'mineen, Abdul Al-Sybu has been executed in your name. 

Ibrahims eyes widened, his fury barely concealed as he spoke. Why, oh director, have you killed the Supreme General of the Itiammudian Army? And why do you proclaim this act in my name when I have not ordered such?

 Ahsan replied choosing his words carefully, the slightest misstep could mean his own execution. He had conspired with the Sybu to our east, he leaked state secrets unto them and likewise planned on defecting whenever they raised their own mighty host to wage a war of complete destruction against us once more.

Ibrahims fury dimmed before he spoke Do you have proof? Ahsan at once turned to Hasan and whispered to him. Hasan produced a file from within a pocket inside his cloak and handed it to the Sealiph before returning to his place in front of his fellow order members.

Ibrahim took the file examining it with all the rigour of a man possessed by a scholar reading poems of his apprentice. He flipped each page meticulously examining the evidence placed before him. He looked up. You have done good in my name. All the fury was gone now he was calm once more. 

The director and grandmaster both bowed in thanks and reverence. Ibrahim called Irman the Stern to his side. He talked with him for a moment and they seemed in agreement about whatever they spoke of. Irman spun around and stood facing forward next to the throne. 

Ibrahim addressed the room. It is your duty, by my decree, that you hunt down every member of the tribe al-Sybu in Irocco and bring me their head. They can not be permitted to take unto themselves the task that their father had begun. 

The delegates nodded and bowed once more before they turned and left the throne room. The tribe that betrayed the Sealiphate would be brought to sunder, by his decree.
-
Ibrahim laid in bed, it was late but he could not rest, all his old decisions seemed to haunt him now. When he so proudly accepted Abdul al-Sybu into his court all those years ago when all was glory and he made sweeping reforms with his beloved wife and his greatest advisor by his side.

But they were all dead now and he was alone, vultures circled his throne but Irman cast them away though he himself sought to bear the seal. Perhaps he should endorse Irman, he was hard to get along with some days but he was a fine man and he would make a great Sealiph even if he is not one of his own children.

Every day that passed he felt the vice of indecision closing around him. He would not sleep well that night, he would not sleep well for a hundred nights. Not until Sybu was wiped from his maps.
[/i]

[/spoiler]

POV: Director Lena Kael, Etherniasti Internal Security Division
March 25, 2025  Fort Verdigo Detainment Facility, Etherniasti[/b]

I walked through the steel corridors of Fort Verdigo, flanked by two guards in full combat gear. The sound of my boots echoed through the concrete halls. The lights above flickered oncea reminder we were still running the facility in lockdown mode.

Five prisoners. All captured after the naval skirmish in the Southern Waters, each of them tied to the Sal-Baliz extremist cell responsible for the Port Thriump missile attack.

Their interrogation had begun three days agoslow, deliberate, careful. No torture, no inhumane tactics. Etherniasti doesn't lower itself to that. But we press hard. We dig deep.

The guards saluted as I stepped into the secure observation chamber. Through the reinforced glass, I could see one of the prisonersmale, early 30s, lean, calculating eyessitting quietly in the center of the room. His name was Sahir Talahn, likely an alias. He hadnt spoken much.

Until today.

He asked to speak to a representative of Hydronia, said Agent Venn, handing me a transcript.

I scanned the report. His message was brief, but chilling:

> You think youve won. You have no idea whats coming. We were just the opening act.

Another prisoneryoung woman, mid-20s, identified as Yena Farashwas beginning to crack under psychological pressure. Shed slipped up earlier, referring to something called The Second Wave. We didnt know what it meant. Yet.

We had already offered to hand the prisoners over to Hydroniaa calculated move. Let them see the inside of one of their black sites, let them face the consequences of aiding a state-sponsored attack on civilians. But the foreign ministry advised we waitsee what more we could extract first.

I stepped into the viewing room, eyes fixed on Sahir. He glanced toward the mirror, knowing I was watching. His expression didnt changecalm, eerily calm.

Send in the interrogator, I said quietly. And bring in the dossier from the Cyber Defense Unit. I want to know if anything they said lines up with the breach from yesterday.

The war with Sal-Baliz was being fought on sea, land, and air. But here?

Here we were in a different kind of battle.

And the prisoners knew something.

Something we hadnt seen yet.
